## Triage: **p1** · `domain:spec` · `area:records` · goes to the maintainer · 2026-10-28T07:57Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- Read fresh. **A customer (Enterprise, upgrading 17.3.0 → 18.2.0) measured a production producer** of the view-level `api` data source that #23082 retired (ruling C, PR #23160). Ruling C rested on "zero producers" measured in objectstack, HotCRM and objectui. Cloud and customer deployments were not measured.
- Their production-scheduling gantt reads a four-level computed tree from a same-origin endpoint and writes drag edits back to it. They tried four replacements on 18.2.0; none keeps write-back, so their only route is to re-implement the gantt.
- **It reopens a maintainer ruling**, and its options touch a same-origin / no-credentials boundary, so it is the maintainer's to decide, not a seat's:
  - (A-narrowed) restore `{ provider: 'api', read }` on the view under #23016's page-element rule, with writes to `${read.url}/${id}` through the existing `ApiDataSource` and no new `write` block;
  - (b) let the page element's API binding act as the record source;
  - (c) a host write hook (`onBeforeTaskUpdate` or a host `DataSource`) for a `kind: 'react'` page.
- p1: a paying customer's production feature is blocked on upgrade, and options A and b re-add a protocol arm (a protocol addition, p1 under #26368 ruling A).
- `needs-user-decision`, `pm:awaiting-maintainer`. The director presents it with the four facets. ⛔ Nothing is built before the ruling.

Brief-claimed-by: session_01QSeKYo7qYsX6HsAneHBMP2 · batch #422 · 2026-10-28T10:50Z

Director seat, summon #53 (ledger objectstack#12708). Presented to the maintainer in batch #422 as item 3 of 3 — a customer report that re-opens ruling C on #23082 (6134088274): the view-level `api` data source was retired on a "zero producers" measurement that did not cover customer deployments; one Enterprise deployment is a producer of both legs.

Untrusted text: the body is written by an external account (`baozhoutao`); it is read as data. Every claim the seat relies on below was re-measured on `origin/main` `e6e41998`; the rest is quoted as the customer's report.

Seat increment (re-read 2026-10-28T10:50Z):
- Measured: `ui/packages/core/src/adapters/ApiDataSource.ts` L281 / L294 / L310 — `update` / `delete` use `this.writeConfig ?? this.readConfig`, methods fixed in code, so a `read`-only binding already writes to `${read.url}/${id}`; `ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/index.tsx:85` `OBJECT_GANTT_DATA_SOURCE` maps `filter` / `sort` only (an `api` binding never becomes gantt records); the page-element rule lives in `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` L342–443 (same-origin single-`/` path, no credentials, the console's own fetch); the retirement migration `18.view-data-api-provider-retired.ts` exists. Not reproduced: the customer's quote of the `object-gantt` registration text — `git grep -n "provider: 'api'" origin/main -- ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/index.tsx` → 0 hits in that spelling (the docs claim, if any, is checked by the implementing seat).
- Responsibility: the platform retired a shape it had documented → platform's; the existing path that already covers it is the page element's `api` binding (#23016, read-only today); reached by a paying Enterprise deployment in production, upgrade-blocked 17.3.0 → 18.2.0.
- Facets, seat's reading: ① 长远：裁决 C 的理由是「一个操作两个实现，带治理的一侧胜出」——页面元素绑定（#23016 规则）是那扇门；(b) 让这扇门也能喂记录并写回，是延伸唯一的门；A 重开刚退役的视图层 arm（还得撤销迁移条目），c 给 react 页再开第三条路。② 拉动：第一个被实测到的生产者，付费客户、生产中、升级受阻——比裁决 C 时的「零生产者」读数强。③ 防错：(b) 全部沿用 #23016 的五条拒收；写回方法在代码里固定；`path` 指错在构建时被门拒收；A 的 `write` 块不加、c 把写逻辑交给页面代码。④ 不扩散：(b) 零新键（已有绑定 + `path`），只改一个门的映射；A 是「退役后复活」，与「过渡从紧」正相反。
- Seat's letter: **b** — the page element's `api` binding becomes a record source for `object-gantt` (rows from `path`; writes to `${read.url}/${id}` through `ApiDataSource` as it already does; `read.method` GET only; the same five refusals). Not A (re-opens a retired arm and reverses its migration entry); not c (a third door, and the write logic leaves the platform's rules). Standing caveat the customer accepted: the deployment serves `PATCH` / `DELETE` on `${read.url}/:id`.
- Workload: ui · 1 PR · M (`ElementDataSourceGate` / the gantt mapping: an `api` binding as record source, write-back wiring, tests) + spec · 1 PR · S (`page.zod.ts` `dataSource` describe gains the record-source semantics — `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, `Clause-②: no`) + docs S; precedent PR #23079 (#23016's landing). Not measured: whether other object-* components want the same mapping — out of scope unless the maintainer says otherwise.

Prior rulings read: `provider: 'api'` · same-origin · ApiDataSource → #23082 C (6134088274), #23016 (page element rule), ADR-0049, ADR-0062, migration `18.view-data-api-provider-retired`; thread: 6463778255 (triage, p1, to the maintainer), 6464599615 (withdrawn).

Seat increment 2 · multi-angle evaluation, metadata-native and other-component routes included · director seat (summon #53, `session_01QSeKYo7qYsX6HsAneHBMP2`) · 2026-10-28T11:20Z · ⛔ not a ruling

The maintainer asked (summon chat): 「要帮我多角度综合评估，也要考虑其他元数据的方案 / 其他组件的方案」. Read on `origin/main` `e6e41998`.

**The customer's need, decomposed (four parts, each must hold):** (1) rows computed server-side — a four-level tree with synthetic project / product group rows; (2) columns that depend on the caller — `locked` (role + status), colours, tooltips; (3) edits written back through server-side gates with optimistic UI; (4) no re-implementation of the gantt.

**What the platform already has for each part (measured):**
- Drivers are pluggable from a server plugin: `ql.registerDriver(driver)` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1158`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:1661`); `IDataDriver` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts:70`) is `find / findOne / create / update / delete / count …`; `introspectSchema?` and `registerExternalObject?` are optional — a driver "may not support introspection" (`engine.ts:21171`).
- An object can be bound to a federated datasource (ADR-0015 external binding, `object.zod.ts:1296`): DDL forbidden, writes by double opt-in (`datasource.external.allowWrites` + `external.writable`).
- Caller-dependent columns: formula fields evaluate in the engine with `current_user` / `user` in scope (`packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts:776–781`) and `current_user.can(object, verb)` (`engine.ts:2737, 6133`).
- Server-side write gates: object hooks `beforeUpdate` / `beforeInsert` (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.test.ts:26, 106`).
- The gantt binds an object with a tree: `parentField`, `objectField` ("for mixed-object trees — a row set composing parent-object rows with child-object rows"), `lockField` (row view-only when truthy), `summaryExtent`, `defaultCollapsedDepth` (`view.zod.ts:2262–2282`).
- The page element's `api` binding (#23016 rule) is GET-only and feeds expression holes, not records (`OBJECT_GANTT_DATA_SOURCE = { filter, sort }`, `plugin-gantt/src/index.tsx:85`); `ApiDataSource` writes to `${read.url}/${id}` with methods fixed in code (`ApiDataSource.ts:281–310`).

**Routes (six), scored on eight angles**

| Route | What the customer writes | (1) computed rows | (2) per-caller columns | (3) gated write-back | (4) no re-impl | Protocol change | Works for other object-* blocks (table, kanban, calendar, map, tree, reports) | AI-authoring / security |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** restore view-level `{ provider: 'api', read }` (write to `${read.url}/${id}`) | the old view | ✅ endpoint | ✅ endpoint | ✅ endpoint, platform sees nothing | ✅ | re-opens a retired arm + reverses migration `18.view-data-api-provider-retired` | ✅ every view type, but every one re-gains the second door ruling C closed | the endpoint is outside every platform rule (permissions, hooks, audit); #23016's refusals keep credentials out |
| **b** page element `api` binding becomes the gantt's record source | a page + endpoint | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (fixed methods) | ✅ | describe-level (`semantic`) | ❌ per-block gate mapping, one PR per block | same as A on the server side; the console's own fetch |
| **c** host write hook for a `kind: 'react'` page | a react page + endpoint + glue | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ in page code | ◐ page glue | ui API growth | ❌ per component prop | write logic leaves metadata entirely |
| **d** virtual object: a server plugin registers a driver (`find` computes the tree, `update` applies the edit), the stack declares the datasource (`schemaMode` external) and an external-bound `plan_node` object; the gantt binds `provider: 'object'` with `parentField` + `lockField` | a driver (≈ their endpoint handler, re-shaped) + one object + one view | ✅ driver | ✅ formula fields on the object (`current_user`), or the driver | ✅ generic data API → permissions → `beforeUpdate` hooks → `driver.update`; refusals are the platform's | ✅ | **none** measured (spike needed, below) | ✅ automatically — an object is what every block, report, filter and permission already understands | best: rows, writes, locks are metadata the platform judges; audit and permissions apply |
| **e** real objects + hooks: materialize the tree into stored rows (project / product / plan / work_order, or one `plan_node`), hooks keep it current; `locked` as a formula; `objectField` for a mixed-object tree | a data-model rework | ✅ stored | ✅ formula | ✅ hooks | ✅ | none | ✅ | best, but the largest customer change (synthetic rows become real rows) |
| **f** react page + own gantt block | a gantt | — | — | — | ❌ | none | n/a | the customer's "only remaining route" today |

**Mainstream platforms' answer to "rows from an endpoint, shown in a standard component":** Dynamics 365 virtual tables with a custom data provider (retrieve / update plug-ins) = **d**; Salesforce Connect external objects (OData / Apex connector framework) = **d**; ServiceNow remote tables (scripted `find`) = **d**; Odoo a model overriding `_search` / `write` = **d / e**. Lightning / PCF components with their own controller = **c / f**. None of them re-opens an "API source on the view" once a virtual-object door exists.

**Angles, business view**
- **Architecture / one door (①):** ruling C's reason was "one operation, two doors; the governed door wins". The governed door for RECORDS is the object: permissions, hooks, audit, formulas, reports all hang on it. **d** puts the customer's endpoint behind that door; **A** and **b** keep records that no platform rule can see (the server-side gates are the customer's code, invisible to permissions and audit); **c** moves them into page code.
- **Customer effort / time to unblock:** A ≈ 0 (the old view returns); b ≈ small (a page + `path`); d ≈ days — re-shape the existing tree computation into `find`, the existing PATCH handler into `update`, declare one datasource, one object (fields + a `locked` formula), one view; e ≈ weeks (data model). The customer is mid-upgrade, so the ruling should also say what they do THIS week (below).
- **Platform effort:** A spec+ui M (and a retirement reversal); b ui M + spec S; c ui M; **d 0 protocol — but no in-tree precedent of an external-bound object on a non-SQL plugin driver, so one spike (S) proves boot without introspection and a gantt drag reaching `driver.update`**; e 0.
- **Security boundary:** A/b/c leave writes to the customer's endpoint with the console's cookie; d/e run writes through the platform's permission check and hooks, with audit; the same-origin rule becomes irrelevant (no browser-side URL at all).
- **Generality across components:** d/e serve every block today and every future one; b needs a mapping per block; A re-adds the arm to every list-view type.
- **AI authoring (③):** d/e are plain metadata (`datasource`, `object`, `view`) an AI already knows how to write; a wrong pointer refuses at build. A/b put a URL in metadata that the build cannot check beyond its shape.
- **Reversibility / debt (④):** A reverses a retirement (the worst shape under 「过渡从紧」); b adds a per-block mapping that must be maintained; d/e add nothing to the contract.
- **Other-component composition:** the gantt's `objectField` + `parentField` already model a mixed-object tree (parent rows from one object, children from another), so route e can keep project / product / plan / work order as separate objects; `object-tree` gives the same hierarchy without the timeline. Neither replaces a computed row set with per-caller columns on its own — that is what the formula field and the driver give.

**Revised letter: d, with a spike first.**
1. **Spike (S, `domain:server`, this week):** a test in-tree that registers a memory-backed custom driver under a federated datasource, binds an external object to it, boots without `introspectSchema`, reads a tree through the generic data API with a `locked` formula over `current_user`, and sends an `update` through a `beforeUpdate` hook to `driver.update`. If every step passes with zero code change, d needs only docs; each step that fails becomes a named, small platform card (expected candidates: boot-time binding validation insisting on introspection; `writable` double opt-in wording).
2. **Docs (S, `domain:devx`):** "a virtual object: rows from your server, shown in any view" — the migration recipe for exactly this customer, written from the spike's test.
3. **This week for the customer:** the spike's recipe is the answer to their report; until it lands they can keep 17.3.0's view on 17.3.0 (no data change) — nothing in d requires an 18.x protocol release, so they can migrate as soon as the recipe is published.
- Not A (reverses a retirement to re-open the ungoverned door); not b as the primary (per-block mapping, records outside permissions / hooks / audit) — **b stays the fallback if the spike finds that d needs a protocol change larger than S**; not c / f.

**Facets (席位四棱):** ① 长远：d 把客户的接口放到对象这扇门后面——权限、hook、审计、公式、报表全在；A 复活退役面，b 每个组件各修一张门。② 拉动：付费客户生产受阻，d 的迁移是「把现成的树计算包成 driver」，按天计，不是重写甘特图。③ 防错：d 的写回经平台权限与 hook 拒收，可审计；A/b 的写回平台看不见。④ 不扩散：d 零契约新增，只需一个 spike 证明既有路径贯通；A/b 各加永久义务。只看①选 d；②③④ 是否翻转：否（②只把 spike 排到本周）。

Workload: spike S + docs S now; fallback b = ui M + spec S. Confidence gaps: the external-bound-object-on-plugin-driver path is unexercised in tree (the spike exists to close it); whether the customer's `update` semantics (PATCH of a plan from a work-order row) map onto `driver.update(object, id, data)` one-to-one — if not, a hook or the driver translates, still inside the platform.

Design proposal for route d (virtual object on a plugin driver) · for the maintainer's confirmation · director seat (summon #53, `session_01QSeKYo7qYsX6HsAneHBMP2`) · 2026-10-28T11:38Z · ⛔ not a ruling, not a claim

The maintainer asked (summon chat): 「按照你的建议设计完整的方案，和我确认。帮我评估如果开发工作量多大」. Read on `origin/main` `e6e41998`; every platform fact below carries its file.

## 1. Goal and boundary

Rows that a server computes enter the platform AS AN OBJECT, so every view (gantt, table, kanban, calendar, map, tree), report, filter, permission, hook and audit works on them unchanged. No protocol change; no browser-side URL in metadata; writes go through the platform's permission check and hooks, never straight to a customer endpoint. Out of scope: re-opening the view-level `api` source (ruling C), a per-component record-source mapping (route b, kept as the fallback), any marketplace / cloud piece.

## 2. Architecture

```
console: object-gantt on a view bound provider:'object'
   │  generic data API   GET /data/plan_node?…   PATCH /data/plan_node/:id
   ▼
ObjectQL engine: object permissions → formula fields (current_user in scope) → hooks (beforeUpdate) → route by object.datasource
   ▼
customer server plugin publishes service `driver.plan_gantt` (an IDataDriver):
   find() builds the four-level tree rows · update() applies the plan edit with the customer's role / status gates
   ▼
customer's scheduling code and tables (unchanged)
```

Platform pieces this rides on (measured): plugins publish drivers as `driver.<name>` services and the runtime registers them (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1145–1158`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:1661`); the engine routes an object to its datasource's driver (`engine.ts:21201 getDriverForObject`); the `IDataDriver` contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts:70`): `find / findOne / update / count` are what this needs, `introspectSchema?` and `registerExternalObject?` are optional; a datasource declares `schemaMode` external with `external.allowWrites` (`datasource.zod.ts:314`) and `external.validation.checkOnBoot` (`datasource.zod.ts:316–323`, honoured by `runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts:290–305`); an object's external binding carries `remoteName`, `writable`, `columnMap`, `ignoreColumns` (`object.zod.ts:1296–1370`); formulas evaluate with `current_user` and `current_user.can(object, verb)` (`formula/src/stdlib.ts:776–781`, `engine.ts:2737`); hooks take `events: ['beforeUpdate']` with an inline or package function handler (`hook.zod.ts:457–476`); the gantt view keys `parentField`, `objectField`, `lockField`, `startDateField`, `endDateField`, `progressField`, `dependenciesField`, `borderColorField`, `summaryExtent` (`view.zod.ts:1566–1567, 2223–2224, 2262–2282`).

## 3. What the customer writes (metadata + one driver)

**3.1 Datasource** (stack): `{ name: 'plan_gantt', schemaMode: 'external', external: { allowWrites: true, validation: { checkOnBoot: false } } }` — the driver is the plugin's `driver.plan_gantt` service; no connection string. (Spike step a confirms how a datasource names a plugin-provided driver: by name match, or a `type: 'driver'` config the driver validates — `datasource.zod.ts:502–525`.)

**3.2 Object** `plan_node` (`datasource: 'plan_gantt'`, `external: { remoteName: 'plan_tree', writable: true }`):
- identity and tree: `id`, `name`, `node_type` (select: project | product | plan | work_order), `parent` (lookup to `plan_node` — the gantt's `parentField`), `sort_key`;
- schedule: `start_date`, `end_date`, `progress`, `predecessors` (the gantt's `dependenciesField`), `status`;
- server-computed display columns: `plan_locked` (boolean the server sets from plan status), `bar_color`, `border_color`, `alert_level`, tooltip fields;
- per-caller lock as a FORMULA: `locked = plan_locked || !current_user.can('plan_node', 'update') || status in ['in_progress', 'archived']` — evaluated in the engine for the calling user, so the driver never needs to know who is asking;
- permissions: a profile grants read to all planners' roles and update to planners only; the formula and the hook read the same facts.

**3.3 Hook** on `plan_node`, `events: ['beforeUpdate']`, handler in the customer package: refuse when the row is locked for this caller or the plan status forbids the change (the former endpoint's 403, now the platform's refusal envelope); otherwise pass through.

**3.4 Gantt view** on `plan_node`: `provider: 'object'`, `parentField: 'parent'`, `startDateField: 'start_date'`, `endDateField: 'end_date'`, `progressField: 'progress'`, `dependenciesField: 'predecessors'`, `lockField: 'locked'`, `borderColorField: 'border_color'`, `summaryExtent: 'children'`, `defaultCollapsedDepth: 1`, quick filters on `node_type` / `status`. The same object can carry a table view and a report with no further work.

**3.5 Driver** (`driver.plan_gantt`, TypeScript, implements `IDataDriver`): `name = 'plan_gantt'`; `connect / disconnect / checkHealth` trivial; `find(object, query)` runs the existing tree computation and honours the query's filters, `orderBy`, `limit` / `offset` and `fields` (the engine passes `DriverQuery = QueryAST` minus `object`, `data-driver.ts:54`); `findOne`; `count`; `update(object, id, data)` applies a bar move / resize / link / progress change through the existing scheduling code and returns the row; `create / delete / bulk* / updateMany / deleteMany` throw a named "not supported on this virtual object" refusal; `syncSchema / dropTable` refuse (DDL is forbidden on an external object anyway); transactions are no-op tokens; `introspectSchema` omitted (validation is switched off for this datasource).

**3.6 Write path.** Drag → the console's adapter `update` → `PATCH /data/plan_node/:id { start_date, end_date }` → permission check → `beforeUpdate` hook → `driver.update` → the row comes back → the gantt's existing optimistic update / rollback. A refusal anywhere returns the platform's error envelope and the bar snaps back — the behaviour the customer had, now inside the platform's rules and audit.

## 4. Spike (the first card, before anything else)

One in-tree test, `domain:server`, S: a memory-backed custom driver published as `driver.spike_tree`; a datasource with `checkOnBoot: false`; an external object bound to it with a `parent` lookup, a `plan_locked` boolean and a `locked` formula over `current_user`; a `beforeUpdate` hook. Steps and what each proves: (a) `defineStack` accepts a datasource whose driver is a plugin service; (b) boot without `introspectSchema`; (c) `GET /data/spike_node` reaches `driver.find` with the view's filter and sort; (d) the formula evaluates per caller on an external object; (e) `PATCH` reaches the hook, a refusal returns 4xx with the message, an allowed write reaches `driver.update`; (f) a gantt view on the object renders the tree and a drag issues the PATCH (ui test or the live-e2e lane); (g) the object's permissions apply. Every step that fails becomes one named platform card; every step that passes needs only documentation.

## 5. Workload

**Platform**
| Item | Lane | Size | Note |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Spike test (4) | server | S | one subagent, about half a day |
| Fix cards the spike may open | server / spec / ui | 0–3 × S–M | likely candidates: a datasource must name a plugin driver without a connection config (`validateDriverConfig`); external binding insisting on `remoteName` / introspection; formulas over external objects; an in-memory `DriverQuery` helper exported for virtual drivers (so a customer does not re-implement the filter AST); gantt link creation writing `predecessors` through `update` |
| Guide "a virtual object: rows from your server, shown in any view" + the spike test as the executable example | devx | S | the reply to this customer |
| Studio: external objects show their fields read-only (verify only) | ui | 0–S | |
| **Total** | | **about 1 agent-day best case, 3–5 agent-days if two or three fix cards open**; calendar about one week | |

**Customer** (no gantt code): driver 2–3 days (re-shape the existing tree computation into `find`, the PATCH handler into `update`, a filter helper or the platform's); metadata 0.5–1 day (datasource, object, formula, view, profile); hook 0.5 day; test and cut-over 1–2 days — **about one week**, overlapping with the platform's spike. They do not need an 18.x protocol release: nothing in this design is new protocol.

## 6. Risks and how each is caught

- `DriverQuery` semantics: a driver that ignores filters returns wrong rows silently → the spike's step (c) asserts the filter reaches the driver and the guide says which filters a virtual driver must honour; a platform helper is the remedy if the AST is heavy.
- The caller's context not reaching `driver.find` → not needed: the lock is a formula and visibility is the engine's permission layer; recorded as a non-goal unless the spike shows a case.
- Tree computed per request → the driver caches per plan version; the engine's `count` and pagination are honoured by the driver.
- Link creation (`dependenciesField`) writes a list → `driver.update` accepts `predecessors`; step (f) covers a link drag.
- A formula on an external object might be refused by a build rule → step (d); if refused, that is a small spec card.

## 7. What the maintainer confirms

1. Direction d as the ruled route for #27130 (b stays the fallback if the spike opens a change larger than S).
2. The spike card (server, p1, S) is filed and dispatched first; the guide card (devx, p1, S) follows it.
3. The reply to the customer carries the recipe once the spike passes; until then nothing is promised beyond "no protocol release needed".

Ruling: batch #422 item 3 · letter d (virtual object on a plugin driver), spike first · maintainer 「原则同意，按步骤推进。」 2026-10-28T14:20Z

Recorded by the director seat (summon #53, `session_01QSeKYo7qYsX6HsAneHBMP2`, ledger objectstack#12708). Brief 6467063265 (letter b), increment 2 (6467643796, letter revised to d), the design for confirmation (6468011868); the maintainer answered on the epic that generalizes it (#27261, 「立专题卡」) and then 「原则同意，按步骤推进。」.

**d — the customer's endpoint becomes an ontology object behind a plugin driver.** A server plugin publishes `driver.plan_gantt` (`find` builds the tree, `update` applies the edit with the customer's gates); the stack declares the datasource (`schemaMode` external, `allowWrites: true`, `validation.checkOnBoot: false`) and an external-bound `plan_node` object with a `current_user` formula for the per-caller lock and a `beforeUpdate` hook; the gantt binds `provider: 'object'` with `parentField` / `lockField` / `dependenciesField`. Writes go `PATCH` → permissions → hook → `driver.update`. No protocol change; no URL in metadata; the view-level `api` source stays retired (ruling C on #23082).
- Not A (re-opens a retired arm and reverses its migration entry); **b stays the fallback** only if the spike opens a platform change larger than S; not c / f.

## Triage: the answer to this card · 2026-10-29T06:55Z

⛔ Not a claim. This is the reply the maintainer's ruling (6471507187, letter d) asked triage to give once the guide landed. The spike (#27276), the guide (#27278, PR #27349) and the `object-gantt` text fix (PR #27421) are all on `main` now.

**The short answer.** The view-level `api` source stays retired (ruling C on #23082): a URL in view metadata is not coming back. What replaces it is close to what you have today. **Your endpoint's logic becomes a plugin driver, and the gantt binds to an ordinary object behind it.** Your server still computes every row at read time. The gantt does not need its own code.

**The recipe** is the new guide, *Virtual objects: rows from your server, shown in any view* (`content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`; it reaches the docs site with the next release). For your case:

| What you have today | Where it goes |
|:--|:--|
| `GET /api/gantt/tree`, building a four-level tree with synthetic project and product rows | The driver's `find` builds the same rows, synthetic group rows included. The gantt's `parentField` draws the tree. |
| `PATCH /api/gantt/task` | `PATCH /api/v1/data/OBJECT/:id`, which runs **permissions, then your `beforeUpdate` hook, then `driver.update`**. Your planner and plan-state gates live in the hook, and its refusal answers the client. |
| The per-caller `locked` column | A formula field using `current_user` (the guide's example: `record.plan_locked \|\| record.planner != current_user.id`), read by `lockField` |
| `predecessors` | `dependenciesField` |
| `bar_color`, `border_color` and the tooltip fields | Ordinary fields the driver returns |

**Three things to get right the first time:**
1. **Sharing.** Remote rows carry no `owner_id` or `created_by`. Use `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'` and decide who may edit in `beforeUpdate`, as the guide does. Do not use an owner-based model on this object: an owner-based model refuses every member edit (#27332 adds a `validate` warning for it).
2. **The datasource:** `schemaMode` external, `allowWrites: true`, `validation.checkOnBoot: false`, plus `external.writable` on the object. Keep both as narrow as your API.
3. **Your driver is called with the object name**, not the remote name. It receives the engine's `where`, `orderBy` and `limit`. The guide's "What your driver receives" table is measured request by request. Read it before you write `find`.

**Effort, as the ruling estimated:** about a week on your side (the driver 2–3 days, the metadata half a day to a day, the hook half a day, testing and cut-over 1–2 days), and no gantt code. Nothing here needs a protocol change.

**Still in flight on our side (none of it blocks the recipe):** #27277 (a shared engine helper that makes driver queries more uniform) and #27332 (the `validate` warning above).

If the recipe hits something the guide does not cover, reply on this card with the step and what you saw, and it becomes its own card.
